No. 9 Tennessee (8-2) hosts LSU (6-4) at Neyland Stadium following a road win over Texas A&M and LSU's 22-21 loss to Texas. Nov. 21, 2:30 p.m. CT. Sources: https://www.secsports.com/news/2026/11/sec-football-on-tv-nov-21 ; https://lsusports.net/sports/fb/schedule/season/2026

setup: No. 9 Tennessee welcomes LSU to Neyland Stadium with the Volunteers at 8–2 after a strong defensive showing in their 22–7 win at Texas A&M. LSU comes in 6–4 after a painful 22–21 loss to Texas. The SEC stakes are different for the two programs: Tennessee is protecting its postseason position, while LSU is trying to break a two-game slide.

things.title: Tennessee's postseason stakes
things.body: The Volunteers are still in the playoff conversation, and their defense just held Texas A&M to seven points. Keeping that physical edge at home is essential as they face another SEC opponent capable of making a one-score game unpredictable.

things.title: How LSU responds
things.body: The Tigers have lost consecutive games to Alabama and Texas, including a one-point finish against the Longhorns. LSU needs steadier offensive execution, fewer empty possessions and the composure to finish opportunities against Tennessee's defense.

things.title: The Neyland factor
things.body: LSU returns to Neyland Stadium for the first time since 2017. Tennessee won the teams' most recent meeting, 40–13 in 2022, but this matchup starts fresh. Crowd pressure and early-down efficiency will matter if the game tightens late.

breakdown.bottom_line: Tennessee brings the stronger recent results and home-field setting, while LSU has the talent and urgency to challenge it. Which team controls early downs, avoids drive-killing mistakes and handles the fourth quarter will shape this SEC test.
